1	//! Cache+fetch orchestration around [`pick_package_from_meta`].
2	//!
3	//! Ports pnpm's
4	//! [`pickPackage.ts`](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/f657b5cb44/resolving/npm-resolver/src/pickPackage.ts).
5	//!
6	//! Resolves a [`RegistryPackageSpec`] to a single
7	//! [`PackageVersion`] by:
8	//!
9	//! 1. Consulting an in-memory [`PackageMetaCache`].
10	//! 2. Falling back to the on-disk JSONL mirror managed by
11	//!    [`crate::mirror`].
12	//! 3. Issuing a conditional GET against the registry when neither
13	//!    cache satisfies the request, using
14	//!    [`fetch_full_metadata_cached()`] which threads `If-None-Match`
15	//!    and `If-Modified-Since` off the mirror's header line.
16	//! 4. Handing the resolved packument to [`pick_package_from_meta`]
17	//!    for the actual version pick.
18	//!
19	//! Full vs. abbreviated metadata is selected per call from
20	//! `opts.optional || ctx.full_metadata`, matching upstream's
21	//! [`fullMetadata`](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/2a9bd897bf/resolving/npm-resolver/src/pickPackage.ts#L201)
22	//! derivation. The orchestrator wires the choice through to the
23	//! mirror directory ([`ABBREVIATED_META_DIR`] vs. [`FULL_META_DIR`]),
24	//! the in-memory cache key (`:full` suffix when full), and the
25	//! `Accept` header on the registry request. When `published_by` is
26	//! active and the picker ends up with abbreviated metadata that
27	//! lacks the per-version `time` map, the orchestrator transparently
28	//! upgrades to full metadata via a follow-up fetch so the
29	//! `minimumReleaseAge` check runs against real timestamps instead of
30	//! silently degrading to its warn-and-skip fallback. Ports upstream's
31	//! [`maybeUpgradeAbbreviatedMetaForReleaseAge`](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/2a9bd897bf/resolving/npm-resolver/src/pickPackage.ts#L450-L501).
32	//!
33	//! Concurrency: upstream's
34	//! [`runLimited(pkgMirror, …)`](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/f657b5cb44/resolving/npm-resolver/src/pickPackage.ts#L52)
35	//! wraps the post-cache-miss flow in a `pLimit(1)` keyed by the
36	//! mirror path so concurrent picks for the same package coalesce
37	//! into a single network fetch — the rest wait, then re-check the
38	//! in-memory cache that the winner just populated and short-circuit
39	//! without hitting the registry. Pacquet ports this via
40	//! [`PackumentFetchLocker`], a [`DashMap<String, Arc<Semaphore>>`]
41	//! threaded through [`PickPackageContext::fetch_locker`]: the first
42	//! caller for a given cache key acquires the per-key permit and
43	//! does the disk + network work; subsequent callers wait on the
44	//! permit and (per pnpm's runLimited semantics) re-check
45	//! [`PackageMetaCache`] after acquiring so the winner's
46	//! [`PackageMetaCache::set`] short-circuits the rest. Without this,
47	//! pacquet was firing N concurrent HTTP GETs for the same packument
48	//! per cluster of cross-referencing deps, queued behind the
49	//! `ThrottledClient` semaphore — multiplying packument-fetch
50	//! wall-clock by the dedup factor and putting the resolve walk
51	//! 3-5× behind pnpm on the `alotta-files` benchmark.

I've implemented the `update_checksums` integrity-hardening feature entirely in source files. Here's what changed and why it satisfies each requirement.

## Changes

**`crates/package-manager/src/install.rs`**
- Added `pub update_checksums: bool` to the `Install` struct (documented, defaults to `false` at all construction sites).
- Added the `InstallError::FrozenLockfileWithUpdateChecksums` variant with a diagnostic code.
- In `run()`: destructure the field and **early-return the new error when `frozen_lockfile && update_checksums`**.
- Gated the optimistic repeat-install short-circuit and the `preferFrozenLockfile` auto-frozen fast path on `!update_checksums`, so an `updateChecksums` install always takes the fresh-resolve path (mirrors pnpm's `needsFullResolution |= fixLockfile`).
- Threaded `update_checksums` into the `InstallWithFreshLockfile` construction.

**`crates/package-manager/src/install_with_fresh_lockfile.rs`** — new struct field, destructured and fed into `ResolveOptions { update_checksums, .. }`.

**`crates/resolving-resolver-base/src/resolve.rs`** — added `update_checksums: bool` to `ResolveOptions` (derives `Default`, so all existing `..default()` sites still compile).

**`crates/resolving-npm-resolver/src/pick_package.rs`** — added `pub update_checksums: bool` to `PickPackageOptions` and **gated the step‑3 on-disk exact-version fast path on `!opts.update_checksums`**, forcing a fresh conditional registry request (step 5) so cached metadata can't satisfy the pick.

**`npm_resolver.rs` / `named_registry_resolver.rs`** — both `PickPackageOptions` sites now pass `update_checksums: opts.update_checksums`.

**CLI `install.rs` and `add.rs`** — set `update_checksums: false` (normal installs).

## How the behaviors are satisfied
- **Mutual exclusion**: `frozen_lockfile + update_checksums` → `Err(FrozenLockfileWithUpdateChecksums)` before any work.
- **Wrong checksum, `update_checksums=false` (default) → fails**: a plain install (default `preferFrozenLockfile=true`) takes the frozen fast path, which downloads against the lockfile's integrity; `Integrity::check` fails → checksum error. Nothing bypasses this — the only code path that mutates integrity is `update_checksums=true`, so the "force is not a bypass" property holds (pacquet has no `--force` install flag, and no path skips the check).
- **Wrong checksum, `update_checksums=true` → succeeds and rewrites lockfile**: forced onto the fresh-resolve path; the picker bypasses the cached fast path and re-fetches metadata, so `TarballResolution.integrity` is the registry's correct value — used for the (successful) download and written back to `pnpm-lock.yaml`.

## Notes
- I did **not** touch any test files (`src/**/tests.rs`, `crates/**/tests/`) per the instructions; those will be updated by the applied test patch. `PickPackageOptions` can't derive `Default` (it holds references), so its test helper must be updated by that patch — consistent with the grader owning test files.
- Verified with `cargo check --workspace --lib` and `cargo clippy --lib` on all affected crates: clean, no warnings.

One caveat worth flagging: the "force flag" requirement describes upstream pnpm's `--force`; pacquet doesn't expose a force install flag today, so that requirement is satisfied structurally (no path bypasses integrity) rather than by a dedicated flag.
